chunks: As for what al-Ḥusayn ibn Muḥammad narrated from Muḥammad ibn Abī Ḥamzah, from Muʿāwiyah ibn Wahb, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, he said:

Jibrāʾīl عليه السلام came to the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم with the times of salat (prayer). He came to him when the sun had declined, and commanded him, so he performed the zuhr salat (prayer). Then he came to him when the shadow had increased by one qāmah, and commanded him, so he performed the ʿasr salat (prayer). Then he came to him when the sun had set, and commanded him, so he performed the maghrib salat (prayer). Then he came to him when the twilight had disappeared, and commanded him, so he performed the ʿishāʾ salat (prayer). Then he came to him when dawn rose, and commanded him, so he performed the subh salat (prayer).

Then he came to him the next day when the shadow had increased by one qāmah, and commanded him, so he performed the zuhr salat (prayer). Then he came to him when the shadow had increased by two qāmahs, and commanded him, so he performed the ʿasr salat (prayer). Then he came to him when the sun had set, and commanded him, so he performed the maghrib salat (prayer). Then he came to him when one-third of the night had passed, and commanded him, so he performed the ʿishāʾ salat (prayer). Then he came to him when the morning had become bright, and commanded him, so he performed the subh salat (prayer).
Then he said: What lies between them is a time.

key_terms.الظِّلُّ: the shadow, used here as a measure for prayer time
key_terms.الْفَجْرُ: dawn, marking the beginning of the morning prayer time
key_terms.زَالَتِ: declined past the zenith, referring to the sun passing midday
key_terms.قَامَةً: a unit of height/length used here to indicate shadow length
key_terms.مَوَاقِيتِ: the prescribed times or appointed timings of acts of worship
key_terms.وَقْتٌ: a valid appointed time for performing the prayer

ai.seo_question: What hadith explains the beginning and ending times of the daily salat (prayer)?
ai.summary: This hadith describes Jibrāʾīl عليه السلام teaching the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم the prescribed times of the five daily salat (prayer) over two days. It shows the earliest and later bounds for these prayer times, indicating that the interval between the two demonstrated times is the valid prayer time.
